source: 19% of people featured on banknotes are Writers (45 people from 23 countries).
claim: 45 individuals from 23 countries are writers, 18.7% of all individuals on banknotes.

source: Writing was the most common profession among women and the second most common for men
claim: Writing is the most common profession among women (14) and the second most common among men (31, behind 37 heads of government).

source: The second most common profession in the dataset is Head of Government, which only features one woman: Corazon C. Aquino
claim: Head of Government is the second most common profession (38 individuals), with only one woman.

source: There are only four female Politicians featured on banknotes and three of them were the first women to hold a specific government role
claim: There are 4 female politicians, 3 of whom are known for being a 'first'.

source: Not a single country we analyzed featured a woman who is considered the founder of their nation.
claim: None of the 25 founders on banknotes is a woman.

source: There are just 12 monarchs featured on banknotes and only two of them are women: Queen Elizabeth II and Queen Tamar of Georgia.
claim: Of the 12 monarchs, 2 are women.

source: In other words, 42% of all the individuals we analyzed can be thought of playing a role in governance broadly defined.
claim: 102 individuals across 34 countries, 42.3% of all individuals, hold governance professions (heads of government, politicians, founders or monarchs).

source: Writers would still be a top profession, coming in second place.
claim: With governance professions combined, writers (45) are the second-largest group after governance (102).

source: On average, 29% of people in a country’s currency were known for being the first ones to do something
claim: 69 individuals (28.6%) are known for being a 'first'.

source: We found that people who were known for a “first” were issued on a banknote sooner than those who were not notable “firsts.”
claim: Individuals known for a 'first' appeared on a banknote 89.9 years after death on average, versus 137.4 years for those not known for a first.

source: Among the 10 people who were alive to see themselves on a banknote, only Queen Elizabeth is still alive today (therefore, she isn’t represented in this graph).
claim: Ten individuals appeared on a banknote while alive: nine died after appearing and one, Queen Elizabeth II, has no recorded death date.

source: 96% of the banknotes were issued after the person on them had died.
claim: 230 of the 239 individuals with a known death date (96.2%) appeared on a banknote after their death.

source: For a third of the featured individuals, it took centuries to get issued on a banknote.
claim: 80 individuals (33.2%) died more than a century before appearing on a banknote.

source: The shortest waiting time for someone to be put on a banknote after their death was just one year, and this was only the case for four people: Gabriel García Márquez of Colombia, General Murtala Mohammed of Nigeria, Corazon C. Aquino and Manuel A. Roxas of the Philippines.
claim: The shortest wait after death was 1 year, shared by 4 people.

source: All four of these people were notable “firsts” as well.
claim: All 4 people with a one-year wait are marked known for a 'first'.

source: Four countries portray an activist and nine others portray revolutionaries who fought to overthrow their oppressors.
claim: Four countries have an activist on a banknote and nine others have a revolutionary.
